transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, thank you for seeing me. I... I'm here because I just can't seem to get my brain to turn off, and it's getting to the point where it's taking over my life. I work in data analysis, you know, mathematical sciences, and precision is everything. But lately, well, not just lately, but it's gotten so much worse... I keep getting these absolutely awful, unwanted thoughts that I’ve missed something critical. 

And it's not just a passing worry like, "Oh, did I lock the door?" It's this overwhelming, crushing feeling that I've made a catastrophic mistake. Like, I'll be at work, and I'll think, "What if I put a wrong number in that data release?" And I know I checked it. I know I did. I have protocols, I have spreadsheets tracking my checks, but my mind just won't let it go. It tells me, "Maybe you looked away for a second. Maybe you hit a key by accident." 

And it bleeds into my home life, too. I'll be driving to work, and suddenly I'm convinced I left the back door unlocked. Not just unlocked, but wide open, and someone is going to break in and it'll be entirely my fault. Or I'll pay a bill, and an hour later I'm terrified I paid it from the wrong account and I'm going to overdraft and ruin my credit and... it just spirals. Even when I *know* I checked the lock, even when I *know* I selected the right account, my mind just won’t let go of the possibility that I’ve caused a complete and utter disaster. It's exhausting. It's just so exhausting to never, ever feel certain about anything I do.

When you have these upsetting thoughts, do you find yourself doing certain things over and over—like checking, counting, or repeating actions—to try to reduce the anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Yes, exactly. I mean, that's exactly what happens. To try and just... calm myself down, to make that crushing feeling stop, I end up doing these routines. Like with work, I will literally close a spreadsheet, tell myself it's done, and then two seconds later, I’m reopening it. And I have to look at the formulas again. And the emails... if I have to send a data report, I will sit there rereading the email line by line, sometimes tracing the words on the screen with my finger, just to make sure I didn't type a wrong number or attach the wrong file. And I do it over and over. 

And it's not just work, it's exactly like you said with the repeating actions. The locks, the bills... I have to check them in this very specific way. Like with the back door, I have to turn the lock, push the handle, pull it back, and I have to do it in a very set order. If I mess up the order, or if my hand slips, or even if it just doesn't feel... I don't know how to explain it, but if it doesn't feel 'safe' inside my head, I have to start the whole sequence over from the beginning. The same goes for the payment confirmations. I'll log into the bank, check the routing number, log out, and then I just have to do it again. And again. Until that 'safe' feeling finally hits. 

It just eats up my entire day, my entire life, really. I mean, some nights, I’m still sitting at my desk hours and hours later. The sun goes down, everyone else has logged off, and I’m just sitting there, reopening the same files, checking the same accounts, and with nothing actually finished. I haven't moved forward on any of my actual work. I'm just stuck in this loop trying to prevent a disaster, and I just can't stop myself until it finally feels right.
